name: Sri Lankan batik and handloom fashion
description: Contemporary Sri Lankan labels built on batik, beeralu lace, handloom and the Kandyan osariya, shown at Colombo Fashion Week.

name: Newar and Dhaka dress revival (Nepal)
description: Nepali revival and fusion of Newar dress and woven textiles (Haku Patasi, Dhaka, Chaubandi Cholo) cut as tailored coats, gowns and waistcoats.

name: Gaucho dress (bombachas de campo)
description: Argentine and Rioplatense horseman dress: bombachas de campo, alpargatas, berets, rastra belts and ponchos, sold by country-wear shops and makers such as Pampero.

name: Antillean madras dress (Wob Dwiyet, robe créole)
description: Creole women's dress of Dominica, Saint Lucia, Martinique and Guadeloupe: white chemise, lace petticoat, madras skirt and head tie, made by local couture labels.

name: Cholita and pollera dress (Andes)
description: Aymara and Quechua women's pollera dress of La Paz and Cusco (gathered skirts, fringed shawls, bowler hats), taken into high fashion by Bolivian and Peruvian designers.

name: Indigenous North American fashion (First Nations, Inuit, Metis, Native American)
description: Indigenous designers of North America blending beadwork, ribbon work, regalia and nation-specific art with contemporary clothing; shown at Indigenous Fashion Weeks in Vancouver, Toronto and Santa Fe.

name: Southeast Asian handwoven textile fashion (songket, tenun, ikat, tais)
description: Contemporary clothing cut from hand-woven songket brocade, tenun, ikat and Timorese tais of Brunei, Malaysia, Indonesia and Timor-Leste.

name: Modern Filipiniana (baro't saya and terno)
description: Philippine national women's dress of baro't saya and terno, reworked by contemporary designers in pina, jusi and local weaves.

name: Khmer sampot and krama
description: Cambodian wrapped sampot and krama cloth in silk and cotton, reworked by contemporary Cambodian labels.

name: Herero dress (ohorokova)
description: Namibian Herero women's long Victorian-style dress with layered petticoats and the horned otjikaiva headdress, sewn by designers for weddings and festivals.

name: Seshoeshoe (shweshwe) dress
description: Dresses, skirts and wraps in discharge-printed shweshwe cotton, worn by married Sotho and Xhosa women and in contemporary South African fashion.

name: Faso Dan Fani fashion
description: Clothing in Burkina Faso's hand-woven Faso Dan Fani cotton strip cloth, from tees and polos to suits and dresses, promoted at Dan'Fani Fashion Week.

name: Kaba and slit (Ghana)
description: Ghanaian women's ensemble of fitted kaba blouse and long slit skirt, made up by couture houses such as Christie Brown and Pistis.

name: Adire and aso-oke fashion (Yoruba)
description: Nigerian labels working Yoruba adire resist-dyed cloth and hand-woven aso-oke, from Maki Oh and Shop Ayora to Kenneth Ize and Deola Sagoe.
